correctness.rationale: Same-side swaps have unchanged utilities and same-type cross-part swaps cannot strictly benefit both. For i on the a-side and j on the b-side of different types, strict cross-multiplied utility gains are exactly d_i=b r_i-a s_i>b and d_j<-a, and force r_i>=2,s_j>=2 so the swap is legal. After the swap d_i decreases by h=a+b and d_j increases by h. Since d_i-h>-a and d_j+h<b, sign classes cannot reverse. The surplus-ticket ceilings P=sum max(0,ceil((d_c-b)/h)) and deficit tickets Q=sum max(0,ceil((-a-d_c)/h)) therefore both decrement by exactly one; a legal swap exists iff both are positive. All maximal trajectories have T=min(P,Q), an equilibrium iff max d<=b or min d>=-a. Each surplus ticket bounded by r_c-1 and deficit by s_c-1, giving T<=min(a-1,b-1), including a=1/b=1.
residual_risks: Fully occupied complete bipartite graphs, nonnegative type populations, fractions of like-type neighbors, strict mutual improvement; no vacancies, non-bicliques, or alternative utilities.
Different maximal sequences need not share the same terminal profile or welfare.
